# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 55 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 55 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_055_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 5, Part 1 — The Vineyard and the Servant

**55:1** "Hear the parable that I am about to tell you, as it pertains to fasting. A certain man had a field and many slaves. And in a certain part of the field he planted a vineyard, and he appointed a certain slave, one who was trustworthy and well-esteemed, as steward over the vineyard, giving him this charge: fence the vineyard, and nothing more, until I return. Keep this commandment of mine, and you shall be free in my household."

**55:2** "And the master of that slave went away abroad. When he had departed, the slave took and fenced the vineyard. When he had finished the fencing, he saw that the vineyard was full of weeds."

**55:3** "He deliberated within himself, saying: I have carried out the lord's commandment — I will now dig this vineyard as well, and when it is dug it will be more attractive; and being free of weeds it will bear more fruit, not being choked by them. So he dug and cleared out all the weeds from the vineyard. And that vineyard became very beautiful and thriving, not being choked by weeds."

**55:4** "After some time the master of that slave and of the field came, and he entered the vineyard and saw that it had been beautifully fenced and also dug, with all the weeds removed and the vine thriving. He rejoiced greatly at what the slave had done, and summoned his beloved son and his friends who were his advisors, and reported to them what he had commanded the slave and what he had found the slave to have done."

**55:5** "And they rejoiced with the master because of the slave. And he said to them: I promised this slave his freedom if he kept my commandment. He has kept my commandment and in addition has done an excellent work for the vineyard, and has pleased me greatly. For this work which he has done, therefore, I wish to make him co-heir with my son, because when he had a good thought, he did not neglect it but carried it through."

**55:6** "The master's son concurred that the slave should be made co-heir with the son. After some days, the master gave a feast and sent many dishes from the feast to the slave. When the slave received the food sent by the master, he took what was sufficient for himself and distributed the rest to his fellow slaves."

**55:7** "His fellow slaves rejoiced when they received the food, and they began to pray on his behalf, that he might find even greater favor before the master, because he had treated them so generously. All these things the master heard and rejoiced greatly at his actions and the generosity of his heart. So the master assembled his friends and his son and reported to them how the slave had dealt with the food he had received; and they were yet more pleased that the slave had been judged worthy of co-inheritance with the son."

---

*LOGOS renders according to the Greek text of P.Mich. 130 with attention to formal correspondence and the christological significance of the vineyard parable.*
